_metadata.notes: Curated seed extract from the SAP Clean Core Extensibility Guide. Each entry distils one canonical rule or pattern. The live PDF fetcher (CleanCoreGuideFetcher live=true) replaces this fixture once a Deloitte-pinned PDF URL is available.

entries.title: Clean Core Level A — Released SAP APIs
entries.description: Level A objects are released SAP APIs and extension points: released CDS interface views (I_*), Released RAP Behavior Definitions (BDEFs) consumed via EML, released BAdIs in published enhancement spots, Application Log (SLG1), Application Jobs (APJ), and the Custom Business Object (CBO) framework. Level A is cloud-ready, upgrade-safe, and the primary target for any new development. Use Level A unless no Level A option exists for the requirement.

entries.title: Clean Core Level B — Classic stable interfaces
entries.description: Level B objects are classic stable SAP interfaces that are supported but legacy: BAPIs, classic BAdIs in customer-namespace enhancement spots, customer exits (USEREXIT_* form routines in named includes such as MV45AFZZ), classic Application Log objects. Level B is acceptable only when a Level A alternative is unavailable. Document the reason for choosing Level B over Level A in the design.

entries.title: Clean Core Level C — Discouraged
entries.description: Level C is direct access to SAP standard objects bypassing released APIs: direct SELECTs on SAP standard tables (VBAK, MARA, KNA1, BKPF, BSEG, etc.), CALL FUNCTION on unreleased function modules, direct INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on SAP standard tables, custom log tables instead of SLG1. Level C is discouraged and must be refactored to Level A/B during code review.

entries.title: Clean Core Level D — Prohibited
entries.description: Level D is modification of SAP standard code: implicit enhancements (ENHANCEMENT without released spot), core modifications via SE38/SE80, custom Z* tables receiving direct INSERTs that duplicate SAP standard data, hallucinated extension points (e.g. references to USEREXIT_ATP_QUANTITY which does not exist). Level D is prohibited and blocks the pipeline.

entries.title: Use RAP Behavior Definitions for transactional writes
entries.description: For any transactional operation on a SAP standard business object that has a released RAP Behavior Definition (BDEF), the code MUST use EML (Entity Manipulation Language) against the BDEF rather than calling the classic BAPI. EML CREATE / UPDATE / DELETE / READ on the released BDEF is Level A; the equivalent BAPI is Level B. Commit work via the COMMIT ENTITIES statement.

entries.title: Use released CDS interface views for all read access
entries.description: All read access to SAP standard data MUST go through released CDS interface views (I_*). Direct SELECTs on SAP standard tables are Level C. Released CDS views provide language-dependent texts, currency conversion, authorization, and stable column contracts across SAP releases. Look up the released CDS view in the SAP Business Accelerator Hub before referencing any SAP standard table.

metadata.replaces: Direct SELECT on SAP standard tables

entries.title: Use EML for all writes on RAP-managed objects
entries.description: Writes to RAP-managed business objects MUST use Entity Manipulation Language (EML): MODIFY ENTITIES OF <BDEF> CREATE/UPDATE/DELETE. Direct INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on the underlying tables is Level C. BAPIs are Level B and acceptable only when no released RAP BDEF exists.

entries.title: Use Application Log (SLG1) for all logging
entries.description: All application logging MUST use the SAP Application Log (transaction SLG1) via BAL_LOG_CREATE / BAL_LOG_MSG_ADD / BAL_DB_SAVE or the CL_BALI / CL_BAL_FACTORY class hierarchy. Custom Z log tables are Level C. Register a custom log object and one subobject per business scenario in SLG0 — for example object Z_DARKHORSE with subobjects Z_BACKORDER, Z_RAP, Z_BATCH.

entries.title: Use Application Jobs (APJ) framework, not classic SM37
entries.description: Background jobs MUST use the Application Jobs framework: implement IF_APJ_RT_RUN and register a job catalog entry via SE80. Classic SM37 / JOB_OPEN / JOB_CLOSE FMs are Level B. Application Jobs run in S/4HANA Cloud, support job templates, and integrate with the Application Log automatically.

entries.title: Prefer released BAdIs over legacy user exits
entries.description: When an extension point is needed, use released BAdIs in published enhancement spots (Level A). Legacy customer exits (USEREXIT_* form routines in includes like MV45AFZZ) are Level B and should only be used when no released BAdI covers the requirement. Hallucinated names such as USEREXIT_ATP_QUANTITY do not exist — the corresponding released BAdI is ATP_CUST_BADI.

entries.title: Side-by-side extensibility on SAP BTP
entries.description: New standalone functionality, integrations, and Fiori apps not covered by S/4HANA standard should run side-by-side on SAP BTP — CAP, RAP-on-BTP, Build Apps, Build Process Automation. Side-by-side extensions communicate with S/4HANA exclusively via released APIs (OData, RAP, Events), keeping the digital core clean. This is the preferred extensibility model for greenfield functionality.

entries.title: In-app extensibility — key user and developer extensions
entries.description: Small changes within S/4HANA should use in-app extensibility: Key User Extensibility (custom fields, custom logic via cloud-shell IDE BAdIs), Custom Business Objects, Custom Reusable Elements. In-app extensions are persisted as released metadata and survive upgrades. Avoid traditional ABAP development in the digital core except where a released RAP BO and in-app option are unavailable.

entries.title: Use the CBO framework for custom persistent data
entries.description: Custom persistent data MUST use the Custom Business Object (CBO) framework — defined via the Custom Business Object app, exposed as a generated CDS view + RAP BDEF + OData service. Direct creation of Z* tables and writing INSERTs to them is Level C and breaks Cloud compatibility. CBOs participate in the standard transactional lifecycle and authorization model.

entries.title: Never write directly to SAP standard tables
entries.description: Direct INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on SAP standard tables (VBAK, BKPF, BSEG, KNA1, MARA, etc.) is Level C — and may corrupt downstream SAP processing. All transactional writes MUST go through released RAP BDEFs (Level A) or, when a BDEF is not available, the corresponding BAPI (Level B). The pipeline flags any direct write to a SAP standard table as a Clean Core violation.
